headline: Intel has joined Applied Materials' new Silicon Valley research centre as a founding partner to work on chipmaking and 3D packaging for AI chips.
score_reason: Lowered 1 from 5: the announcement was made on 6 Oct, before the window, and describes goals rather than results.
importance_line: It aims to shorten the path from lab to US factory for advanced AI chips, which matters to chipmakers and their customers over years, but both firms describe intentions and no results or dates are given.
summary: THE ELEC reports that Applied Materials said on 6 Oct 2026 that Intel has joined its EPIC Center, a Silicon Valley facility for developing chipmaking equipment and processes, as a founding partner to work on new transistor materials, interconnects and Foveros 3D chip-stacking packaging. Applied will give Intel a dedicated secure space linked to Intel's Hillsboro, Oregon, campus; the centre has more than 10 participants, including Samsung, SK hynix, Micron, TSMC and Broadcom, and is due to open on 12 Oct.
notes: Digitimes page (7 Oct) shows only a lead; facts read at THE ELEC and Unite.AI, both rewriting Applied Materials' 6 Oct announcement (Unite.AI quotes both CEOs). Investment is given as 7 trillion won by THE ELEC and $5 billion in Besi/DQ text; not used in summary.
